title: Triage for Degraded Latency and SLO Regression
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This page defines a reproducible investigation and escalation workflow for on-call responders when service latency or SLOs degrade. It prioritizes rapid customer-impact mitigation, data collection for root cause analysis, and clear customer/status communication. Use this document for live incidents where latency, tail latency (P95/P99), or error-rate signals cross SLO thresholds for any Redwood service (hosted API, dedicated pools, private agents).

When to use this guide
- P95 latency for production API endpoints exceeds target by >30% for 5+ minutes.
- Error-rate (4xx/5xx) increases above 2x baseline for 3+ minutes.
- SLO burn rate > 2x and projected to exhaust error budget within 24 hours.
- Significant regional degradation (>= 10% of requests failing or timing out)

Key SLOs and thresholds (examples)
- Hosted API availability: 99.95% monthly.
- Token-generation latency: P50 < 120ms, P95 < 350ms, P99 < 800ms (global).
- Embedding endpoint: P95 < 450ms.
- Error rate: <0.1% global normalized for transient client issues.
- Alerting thresholds in production: P95 > target * 1.3 for 5m => pager.

Primary signals and dashboards
- Redwood Console > Dashboards > Per-route latency (primary).
- Traces: Zipkin/Jaeger service map for top-tier calls (api-gateway -> routing-proxy -> inference-runtime).
- Metrics: Prometheus groups (api.*.request_duration_seconds, model.*.inference_latency_ms, runtime.*.gpu_utilization).
- Logs: Kibana queries scoped to trace_id / request_id.
- Error budget burn: SLO dashboard / SLO-alert channel.

Alert to priority mapping
1. P0 (pager): global client-impacting latency or availability outages, SLO burn rate >= 4x and projected to exhaust within 3h.
2. P1 (pager): sustained P95 > 1.5x target for 15m OR error rate spike > 5x baseline.
3. P2 (ticket/watch): transient spikes that self-correct within 15m or isolated to single non-critical region.

Immediate on-call checklist (first 10 minutes)
1. Confirm the signal
   - Open alerts channel and SLO dashboard. Note the alert firing time and affected routes.
2. Establish initial scope and impact
   - Which routes/endpoints are affected (text-generation, embeddings, health checks)?
   - Which regions and customers are in scope? Use the per-customer metric filter.
3. Mobilize communication
   - Post to #incident-ops with short summary: impact, region, initial mitigation if any, responder name. Use status template below.
4. Switch to focused debugging mode
   - Drop non-essential background tasks (scale down batch jobs if they generate inference load).
5. Collect triage data (commands and queries)
   - Prometheus: api: curl -sS "https://prometheus.internal/api/v1/query_range?query=histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(api_request_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))&start=..."
   - Runtime health: kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=inference-runtime -o wide
   - Top traces: query Jaeger: service=inference-runtime, operation=DispatchRequest, minDuration=200ms
   - GPU health: redwood-monitor query: "runtime.gpu_utilization{pool='dedicated'}"

Investigation ladders (by likely cause)
A. Resource saturation (CPU/GPU/memory/network)\   1. Check node-level metrics: cpu, mem, net.\   2. Check autoscaler logs and pending pods.\   3. If saturation, execute mitigation: increase pool capacity (scale up), or temporarily divert routing to secondary pool.\   Commands: kubectl top nodes | sort -nr -k3\B. Queueing or batching regressions\   1. Inspect inference-runtime queue lengths and latency vs batch size.\   2. If batch sizes spiked, roll back recent batching config or apply immediate cap.\   3. Adjust continuous batching policy: POST /admin/batching-config {"max_batch_size": 8} (use admin CLI).
C. Slow downstream dependency (KV store, auth, routing service)\   1. Trace call stacks to identify slow hops.\   2. Restart or scale the impacted downstream if safe (follow runbook).\D. Regressions from recent deploys (canary/rollouts)\   1. Check deploy timeline: gitlab-ci / release-notes page for recent rollouts in the last 60 minutes.\   2. If a canary is implicated, initiate immediate rollback or emergency canary pause.

Quick mitigation playbook (fast actions to reduce customer impact)
- Circuit-break non-essential features: disable long-polling debug endpoints, reduce logging verbosity, turn off non-critical telemetry.
- Route traffic to a lower-capacity model variant with similar output (e.g., model-x-quantized-v2) to reduce per-token compute.
- Throttle burst traffic via API gateway: set request rate limit to 50rps for affected routes.

Escalation matrix (who to call and when)
- On-call SRE (primary) — immediate pager recipient for P0/P1.
- Runtime team lead (Hannah Cho) — escalate if mitigation not effective in 20 minutes.
- Platform infra (Miguel Ortega) — escalate for capacity/network faults.
- Product owner (model-team) — for model-induced quality regressions or rollouts.
- Customer Success (for named-customer impact) — notify at 30 minutes if customer SLA affected.

Customer communication templates
- Status page short template (use status.redwood.ai):
  Title: Service latency impacting text-generation (region)
  Impact: Degraded response times observed for text-generation endpoints in REGION for approximately X minutes.
  Scope: A subset of customers and routes may experience higher latency or timeouts.
  Current status: Engineers are investigating; mitigation in progress.
  Next update: in 30 minutes or earlier.

- Email / CS template (when notifying customers directly):
  Subject: Incident: higher-than-expected latency for text-generation (REGION)
  Body:
  Hello [Customer Name],

  We are currently investigating an issue causing increased latency for text-generation in REGION. Our engineers have identified scope and are applying mitigations to reduce impact. We will provide an update within 30 minutes and follow up with a full incident report after resolution.

  Owner: Aisha Patel (oncall@redwood.ai)

Post-incident workflow (RCA and follow-up)
1. Containment confirmed and incident declared resolved in #incident-ops.\2. Create incident record in the incident tracker with timeline, key metrics, mitigation steps, and full owner list.\3. Complete a blameless RCA using the template below within 5 business days.\4. Raise follow-up actions (JIRAs) for: code fixes, capacity changes, alert tuning, test coverage (game day).

RCA template (to copy to Confluence incident page)
- Summary (one paragraph):
- Timeline (timestamps, actions, responders):
- Root cause(s):
- Detection and response: what worked / gaps:
- Customer impact (who, how many, duration):
- Action items (owner, due date, validation plan):

Game day scenarios and schedule
- Purpose: validate detection, escalations, mitigation, and communication steps for SLO regressions.
- Suggested quarterly scenarios: simulated P95 spike in a region, sudden GPU node exhaustion, canary-caused latency regression.
- Two-hour game day runbook:
  00:00 — Inject simulated alert; on-call responds and follows checklist.\  00:20 — Execute mitigation (traffic-shift, temporary cap).\  00:40 — Escalate to team lead and practice customer notification.\  01:00 — Stabilize and prepare postmortem notes.\  01:30 — Retro and lessons learned.

On-call rotation & ownership notes
- Primary on-call: SREs rotate weekly (Mon–Sun). Primary owns first-response and triage.\- Secondary on-call: Platform engineer, available for scale and infra actions.
- On-call shadow and handover: at shift start, read the OPEN_INCIDENTS board and confirm runbook versions.

Runbook governance and maintenance
- Update this page after any live incident where the runbook changed.
- Owners must review annually and after every game day.

Appendix: useful queries and links
- Prometheus SLO query examples (copy/paste):
